provenance: Written 2026-10-16 by a FOUNDRY helper from owner rulings only; RM_FlowKernel.cs and the Python oracle were not read. Item: STAGE3 section 7 decision 1.
rules_for_test_writer: Read this file and the world interface only; never the kernel or the oracle.
Never weaken a claim to make it pass. A red is a question for a referee who is neither author.
A scene whose verdict is not 'approve' is not tested. A claim under an open needs_ruling is tested only as its until_ruled line says.
Editing 'scenes' breaks the seal; a changed scene needs the owner's approval again.

legend.~: natural water body that touches the map edge and is large (LIMITLESS, sticky); drawn truncated
legend.P: natural enclosed deep-water pond square (LIMITED); 2 m deep, holds 4,000 L (4 notches) when full
undug ground, depth 0; never holds liquid
legend.1: dug cell 0.5 m deep (1 notch), dry at start unless the scene says otherwise
legend.4: dug cell 2 m deep (4 notches): the pit (SUPERDEEP)
legend.G: sealed sluice gate standing on a depth-1 dug cell
legend.#: metal grate gate standing on a depth-1 dug cell
legend.U: powered pump (unless the step says unpowered)
legend.<: hose free end set to Intake, lying in liquid
legend.>: hose free end set to Outflow, lying in a dug cell

global.units: litres, with depth in metres (design/RimMandrake/flowworks_unified_depth_2026-10-17.md, ruled 2026-10-17). One notch = 0.5 m of water in one square = 1,000 L. Where a claim counts 'levels' (S1-S4, S6) it means notches. A dug cell of legend depth D is D notches (D x 0.5 m) deep and holds 0..D notches.
global.pulse: one step of the liquid engine at its shipped cadence; horizons are UPPER BOUNDS ('by pulse H'), never exact timings
global.settled: no cell's fill changes for 3 consecutive pulses
global.settings: shipped defaults, except: rain off, refill/seepage off, fire off, weather clear. Every dug cell sits well outside the map-edge sink band (ruling 28).

invariants_every_scene.claim: No undug cell ('.') ever holds liquid.
Every dug cell always has 0 <= fill <= depth.

In a scene with no LIMITLESS body and no pump drawing from one, the total of all liquid (cells + ponds + tanks + hoses) never rises, and falls only by an amount the game discloses to the player as destroyed overflow.

excluded_everywhere: how anything looks (art, ripples, fill-tier graphics)
liquids other than water, and viscosity
exact timing inside the horizon, and which of two equally valid cells fills first
rain, season refill and seepage (switched off)

scenes.title: A source-fed 1-deep canal fills end to end
scenes.setup: A large edge-touching lake (LIMITLESS). An 8-cell depth-1 canal, cell 1 touching the lake shore, dug dry; the last dig completes at pulse 0.

rulings.quote: liquid then flows into the canal to fill it, extending the source ... Any source that touches the map edge is determined to be limitless.
Natural sources are treated as SUPERDEEP.
a large body shouldn't be able to 'flap between' because it can't be reduced, it's limitless once and for all.

expected.claim: All 8 canal cells hold 1 level.
At every pulse the wet canal cells form one unbroken run starting at cell 1 (no isolated puddle, no gap).
Once a canal cell is wet it never goes dry again during the scene.
The lake never visibly shrinks (LIMITLESS).

fails_if: the canal stops at its first cell (1,0,0,0,...) and stays there
exclusions: speed per cell within the 10-pulse bound

scenes.title: A shallow trench beside a source-fed pond fills
scenes.setup: The same LIMITLESS lake. A player-dug 2x2 depth-4 pond touching the lake. A 6-cell depth-1 trench leaving the pond's far side; the trench does not touch the lake. All dry at pulse 0.

rulings.quote: Strained isn't a thing anymore. We replaced 'sources' with just placed deep liquid reservoirs just like a player would normally place on the map. Filled very deep tiles. Everything follows from that.
A full cell overflows into neighbours with room ... a natural source is simply a full deep cell that spills into any channel dug at its edge.

expected.claim: All 4 pond cells hold 4 levels.
All 6 trench cells hold 1 level.
Wet trench cells always form one unbroken run starting at the cell touching the pond.
Once settled, nothing in the pond or trench changes for the rest of a 60-pulse run.

fails_if: the pond fills but the trench stays dry
the trench wets only its first cell
exclusions: whether the pond is full before the trench starts
the order the four pond cells fill in

scenes.title: A pump fills a canal that touches no water
scenes.setup: An enclosed natural pond of 12 deep squares (the Intake end lies on one) (LIMITED, 48 levels), not touching any edge. A pump on dry ground; one hose from the pump to the pond with its end set to Intake; one hose from the pump to cell 1 of a 6-cell depth-1 canal with its end set to Outflow. No tank. The canal is at least 2 undug cells from the pond. Step A: pump unpowered for 20 pulses. Step B: pump powered.

rulings.quote: No, intake needs a pump. Adding liquid to any storage takes work (pump). Taking liquid out of storage to the outside world does not (drainage). Use the mental model that all storage is "above" the in-world liquid availability.

How could we also support having a pump suck water from a lake and put it in a disconnected canal? ... we could have one hose be intake, and another be outflow, and the pump does the rest. Wouldn't even need to have a tank in the mix really.
Where fill/empty is set: hose ENDS + tank JOBS (card pick).
We should also have some tests if you don't already showing pumping water between two equal-volume reservoirs through a tank gets you the same water in the end (conservation of volume).

expected.claim: Unpowered: the canal stays dry and the pond keeps all 48 levels.
All 6 canal cells hold 1 level.
Levels gained by the canal plus levels held in the hoses = levels lost by the pond, at every pulse.
The undug cells between pond and canal stay dry (G1).
Variant: two equal dug 3x3 depth-4 reservoirs A (full, 36 levels) and B (empty), pump + one tank between them. Pump A to B, then B back to A. At the end A holds 36 levels, B 0, tank 0, hoses 0.

fails_if: liquid appears in the canal with the pump unpowered
the pond loses less than the canal gains
exclusions: which pond cells give up their water
the shape of A after the round trip (only its total)

needs_ruling.question: A drill (ruling 3, 'part of Many Waters') or the new mapmaker Source tap (2026-10-16) stands beside a dug canal. Does it pour straight into the touching dug cell, or only into a tank/hose network that then needs an Outflow end?

options.a: straight into the touching dug cell
options.b: only into a network; the canal is fed through an Outflow end
options.c: both: it fills the touching cell if there is one, else the network

needs_ruling.until_ruled: the drill/tap variant is not tested

scenes.title: A sluice gate shut, then open, then shut again
scenes.setup: The LIMITLESS lake. A depth-1 canal: 3 cells upstream, a sealed sluice gate on cell 4, 4 cells downstream. Gate shut at pulse 0, canal dry. Step A: 20 pulses shut. Step B: open the gate for 20 pulses. Step C: shut it for 40 pulses. Variant: the same with a metal grate gate, never opened.

rulings.quote: Sluice gates: YES. A buildable gate cell that holds liquid back until opened.
There are sealed sluice gates (standard) and the ones made of metal grates that always allow liquid (this is just a gate, not a sluice gate then). Yes, both, two kinds of door.
Sluice doors and grates may be placed on wet canal cells (card pick).

expected.claim: The 3 upstream cells hold 1 level.
The 4 downstream cells stay dry while the gate is shut.
After opening, all 4 downstream cells hold 1 level.
Shut again: the upstream cells stay full.
Grate gate, never opened: all 4 downstream cells hold 1 level.

fails_if: water passes a shut sealed sluice
exclusions: the fill of the gate's own cell
gate art and which way it turns

needs_ruling.question: Step C: the gate is shut again with the 4 downstream cells full. That water is now cut off from the lake. What should it do?

options.a: stay exactly as it is until the gate opens or a pump/sink moves it
options.b: slowly drain back through the shut gate to the lake (a leaky gate)
options.c: slowly drain away and vanish (evaporation) - this would be a second exception to conservation

needs_ruling.until_ruled: S4 step C makes no claim about the downstream cells

scenes.title: Nothing created or destroyed: a closed pond pays for its canal, by gravity and by pump
grid: .P1111111111...          B: 1-square pond, 2 m (4,000 L); 10-cell 0.5 m canal
.P4............          F: 1-square pond, 2 m; one 2 m canal square
.<====U====>111111.      G: '<' lies on a 1-square pond, 2 m; pump; 6-cell 0.5 m canal
scenes.setup: Nothing touches a map edge. Water moves by the ruled leveling law: it flows only downhill and settles to one surface; a canal takes only water standing above its own floor. Part A: a 3x3 enclosed deep pond (9 squares, 2 m, 36,000 L) and a 10-cell 0.5 m canal dug dry off it, by gravity. Part B: the same canal off a 1-square pond (2 m, 4,000 L), by gravity. Part C: in Part B's end state, fill in canal cell 1. Part D: an isolated 3-cell 0.5 m run, every cell authored full (0.5 m), touching nothing; fill in the middle cell. Part E: an enclosed 6x6 basin 1 m deep with 8,000 L authored as 4 centre cells at 1 m, the rest dry. Part F: a 1-square pond (2 m, 4,000 L) beside one dry 2 m dug canal square, by gravity. Part G: a 1-square pond (2 m, 4,000 L); a powered pump on dry ground; one hose from the pump to the pond, end set to Intake; one hose from the pump to cell 1 of a 6-cell 0.5 m canal, end set to Outflow; no tank. The canal is at least 2 undug cells from the pond.

rulings.quote: Scarcity is stock, not rate ... conservation of mass is true everywhere.
There should also be a way to 'fill in' a canal that displaces liquid BACK. It does not destroy liquid if there's a place for it to go, but if it would 'overflow' it is destroyed.
1 tank square, 1 deep water square/pond, 1 deep canal square should all be the same volume. Right now that's 4 I believe.
It should slosh around until it levels
Please select an algorithm that will allow the fluid to levelset down to a smooth 0 or 1 across a too-wide field like this, not 0, deep, 0

Scheme A: litres are the truth, metres are the ruler, the step is 0.5 m (1,000 L in one square); 'five' is deleted. A pond square's supply has no fixed count: by pump 4,000 L, by gravity only what stands above the canal's floor.
rulings.file: design/RimMandrake/flowworks_unified_depth_2026-10-17.md section 10 (D1 by card; D6 S5 redraw defaulted, veto-able)

expected.claim: Pond + canal always hold 36,000 L. At no pulse are all 10 canal cells wet (at most 9); no canal cell ever holds more than 0.5 m; the wet canal cells are one unbroken run from the pond.
The pond holds less water than at the start (its surface is lower), and never less than 27,000 L: it gives at most its top 0.5 m.
At most one canal cell, cell 1, is ever wet, holding at most 0.5 m; the pond keeps at least 3,000 L; pond + canal = 4,000 L.
The wet front does not move for 40 more pulses.
Filling in cell 1 destroys nothing: canal + pond still hold 4,000 L, and no overflow message appears.
Filling in the middle cell destroys exactly 1,000 L (0.5 m in one square), and the player sees a message that names the amount.
Settled: no cell holds 1 m while any cell of the basin is dry; the wet cells are one connected patch; the total is still 8,000 L.
The pond square and the 2 m canal square settle to one surface: each holds 1 m of water (2,000 L); the total is 4,000 L; nothing changes for 10 more pulses.

Pond + hoses + canal = 4,000 L at every pulse. The pump empties the pond (bar what the hoses hold); the canal ends with cells 1-4 wet at 0.5 m each (cells 1-3 if the hoses still hold water), never a 5th; no undug cell is ever wet.

fails_if: any total changes except Part D's disclosed 1,000 L
Part A ever wets all 10 canal cells, or Part B more than one: water climbing above its own surface
Part F stays unlevel (pond full and canal dry, or the reverse)
Part G wets a 5th canal cell
exclusions: whether Part A's top 0.5 m ends mostly in the pond or in the canal
whether Part C's displaced water lands in the canal or the pond
which 8 basin cells end wet in Part E
how much the hoses hold at any pulse in Part G
the wording of the overflow message

scenes.title: Save and reload mid-flow, and the flow carries on
scenes.setup: S5 Part A, plus S4's gate scene with the gate shut and the downstream half full. Run 1: uninterrupted to pulse 30. Run 2: the same start; save at pulse 4 (canal partly wet), reload, continue to pulse 30.

rulings.quote: Scarcity is stock, not rate ... conservation of mass is true everywhere.

scenes.rulings_note: No owner ruling speaks about save and reload. This scene rests on conservation alone, which is why S6.Q1 exists.

expected.claim: Straight after the reload, every cell's depth and fill, the pond's stock, and the gate's open/shut state equal what they were at the save.
Total liquid in Run 2 is the same before the save and after the reload.
Run 2 ends in the same settled state as Run 1, cell for cell.

fails_if: a fill front that restarts from the mouth after reload
water gained or lost across the reload
a shut gate that comes back open
exclusions: saves made by older mod versions (migration)

needs_ruling.question: After a reload, must the flow be identical pulse by pulse to a run that was never saved, or only end in the same place?

options.a: identical at every pulse (strict; the strongest test)
options.b: same totals and same final settled state; small differences on the way are fine

needs_ruling.until_ruled: S6.c (the final state) is tested; pulse-by-pulse identity is not

owner_verdicts.recorded: 2026-10-17, owner at the keyboard, by question card; recorded by a FOUNDRY helper. Outside the seal. The file was re-sealed the same day for the S5 redraw (see revisions); these answers are unaffected.

S3.Q1.owner_said: If you place it in a canal, it fills the canal. If you place it on the surface, it needs a pipe or hose connection.
S3.Q1.meaning: A drill or Source tap standing IN/touching a dug canal cell pours straight into that canal. On undug surface ground it pours only into a connected pipe or hose network.

S4.Q1.meaning: Water cut off downstream when a sealed gate is shut again stays exactly where it is until the gate opens, or a pump or the map-edge drain moves it.

S5.Q1.answer: resolved 2026-10-17 by the unified depth ruling: no fixed count
S5.Q1.owner_said: We collectively ruled four across everywhere... but then we moved to meters depth and Liters. Please do a full deep design pass right now on how to reconcile all of this. It's ok to have some number of visual depths of liquid, as well as visual depths of canal. But we must not get confused on the depth of the water. So please, come up with a unified way to represent all of this and present it to me. Then let's adjust all the design docs and mechanics once and for all. As for natural sources, yes they should be able to go MUCH deeper than level 4 canals.
S5.Q1.meaning: Scheme A (by card): by pump one 2 m pond square gives 4,000 L = four 0.5 m canal squares; by gravity the leveling law limits it to the water above the canal's floor. S5 is redrawn (parts A, B, F, G) and awaits his re-approval.

S6.Q1.meaning: A reloaded run must match the never-saved run in totals and end state; small differences on the way are fine.

revisions.what: S5 redrawn per the unified depth ruling (D1 Scheme A by card; D6 'both' defaulted, veto-able): A and B keep the 0.5 m canal and claim the leveling-law limits; new F (2 m canal by gravity) and G (pump). Legend and global units restated in metres and litres, meaning unchanged for S1-S4 and S6. S5.Q1 resolved.
revisions.owner_must: re-approve S5 only; his S3.Q1, S4.Q1 and S6.Q1 answers stand
